key_insight: A sample-efficient, model-free robust Q-learning algorithm learns from a single Markovian trajectory, with a theoretical guarantee within a factor of 1/(1−γ) of minimax optimality.
engineering_relevance: The method targets sim-to-real transition uncertainty, offering a route to policies that remain reliable when deployment dynamics differ from the nominal model.
method: Use asynchronous Q-learning in a discounted, infinite-horizon robust MDP.
Model transition uncertainty with total-variation neighborhoods of radius σ.
Learn from one trajectory generated by a behavior policy under nominal dynamics.
evidence_signal: The abstract gives a theoretical sample-complexity bound of Õ(1/[μ_min ε²(1−γ)³ max{1−γ,σ}] + t_mix/[μ_min(1−γ)]) for entrywise ε-accurate optimal Q-values; it reports no empirical evaluation.
watch_item: The bound worsens with poor state-action coverage, slow trajectory mixing, and discount factors near one.
paper_title: Provably Efficient Q-learning for Robust Reinforcement Learning
